en: The Hymn to the Guru and the Three Jewels:
Om, homage to the Three Jewels!
[To that which has] craving for its tongue, false conceptualization for its head, and aversion for its quivering fruit...

Homage to that Buddha who, by the power of wisdom and mantra, pacified the terrible demon whose eyes were fierce with passion, whose face was delusion, whose thoughts exceeded hundreds of millions of his own bodies, and who manifested as desire, anger, and discursive thought. 1.

I pay homage to that glorious Great Awakening—the Buddha, the fully awakened one, the sovereign of the sublime Dharma, the peaceful, the pure, the bestower of equal renown, the mine of virtues, the being who is the king of the lords of sages. (2)
Thus ends the *Buddharatnastotra*.
He who is the eye for virtuous beings scorched by the sufferings of birth and so forth; he who daily draws forth sentient beings from the cage of the triple world.

Homage to that Great Dharma, which rescues the world from the ocean of afflictions and suffering when it is without protection, and which [rescues] the perfectly awakened ones when they have passed away. 3.
That which, through omniscience, leads the Śrāvakas seeking peace to tranquility;
that which, through knowledge of the paths, accomplishes the welfare of the world for those who act for the benefit of beings;
and that which is conjoined with all aspects of the universe—of this the Sages speak.
Homage to that Mother of the Buddha, who is accompanied by a host of Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas. || 4 ||
Thus ends the Hymn to the Jewel of the Dharma.
Four are present in the world, who loathe the sweet taste of the pleasures of existence;
and four abide in the fruit, great yogis who delight in tranquility and are peaceful.
Homage to that Saṅgha, in which the Blessed One—whose body was refined by wisdom, ethical discipline, and meditative concentration—prophesied these eight excellent individuals. (5)
I constantly pay homage to the Buddha, whose hand holds the supreme lotus,
whose nature is loving-kindness, who is Gaganagañja and Samantabhadra,
the lord of yakṣas, and Mañjughoṣa who has cast off all worldly attachments.
I bow with devotion to Viṣkambhin and Kṣitigarbha. || 6 ||
Thus ends the *Saṃgharatnastotra*.
The Buddha is the Guru, the Dharma is the Guru, and likewise the Saṃgha is the Guru;
the glorious Vajradhara is the Guru—to that glorious Guru, homage! (7)
The *Śrī Gururatnatrayastotra* is completed.
